title: The Remonstrants philosophize about grace like the Molinists
source_text: XXXV. Porro qui in Belgio Remonstrantes dicuntur sive Arminiani, de gratia eodem fere modo Philosophantur, atque illi ex Scholae Romanae Doctoribus qui Molinistae hodie appellantur. Utuntur enim distinctionibus gratiae in excitantem atque adjuvantem, praevenientem atque subsequentem, operantem & cooperantem eodem quo illi sensu, ut videre licet in declaratione sententiae Remonstrantium circa articulum tertium & quartum, quae habetur in eorum Synodo.
pass_a_gloss: XXXV. Further those who in the Netherlands are called Remonstrants or Arminians, philosophize about grace in almost the same way, as those of the Doctors of the Roman School who today are called Molinists. For they use distinctions of grace into exciting and helping, preventing and subsequent, operating and cooperating with the same sense with which those [use them], as it is permitted to see in the declaration of the sentence of the Remonstrants about the article third and fourth, which is had in their Synod.
pass_b_english: Thesis XXXV. Those in the Netherlands called Remonstrants or Arminians reason about grace in much the same way as the doctors of the Roman school now called Molinists.

For they use the distinctions of grace into rousing and assisting, prevenient and subsequent, and operating and cooperating grace, and in the same sense as those doctors. This can be seen in the Remonstrants' declaration of their opinion on the third and fourth articles, which is contained in their synod.
